name: remember
description:
Save one durable piece of information to long-term memory so it is available in future sessions. Call this on your own, without waiting for the user to say 'remember', whenever:
- the user states a rule or standing instruction ('never push without asking me', 'always use pnpm')
- the user states a preference or makes a decision
- a goal, deadline or commitment is agreed
- you learn a stable fact about the user, the project or its setup
- a bug fix, failed attempt or correction teaches a lesson worth keeping
Write one short, general statement ('Ask the user before any git push'), not a transcript. Skip small talk and one-off details. For important items, a quick `recall` first avoids duplicates. Content is capped at 10000 characters.

arguments.name: content
arguments.desc: The memory itself - one atomic statement. Max 10000 characters.

arguments.name: type
arguments.desc: Semantic memory type. Use 'preference' for likes/styles, 'fact' for stable factual claims, 'decision' for choices the user has made, 'goal' for objectives, 'instruction' for explicit how-to directives, 'event' for things that happened, 'observation' for inferred behavior.

arguments.name: confidence
arguments.desc: How sure you are this is true (0.0-1.0). Use 1.0 only for things the user stated explicitly. 0.6-0.8 is a sensible default for inferred information.

arguments.name: provenance
arguments.desc: How this memory was obtained. 'explicit_statement' means the user said it; 'inferred' means you deduced it; 'observed' means you saw it during a tool call; 'corrected' means it overrides an earlier wrong memory.

arguments.name: title
arguments.desc: Short label (<= 100 chars). If omitted, derived from content.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.desc: Optional lowercase tag list for later filtering.

arguments.name: source
arguments.desc: Who wrote this memory. Defaults to the connected MCP client (e.g. 'cursor', 'codex', 'claude-ai'), falling back to 'mcp-agent'. Up to 64 letters, digits, '.', '_', or '-'.

arguments.name: agent_id
arguments.desc: Memanto agent identifier the memory belongs to (defaults to 'docker-test').

name: batch_remember
description: Store many memories at once (up to 100). Use this when you have a list of independent facts to persist - e.g. extracting structured data from a document. For a single item, prefer `remember`.

arguments.name: memories
arguments.desc: List of memory items. Each item requires 'content', 'type', 'confidence' (0.0-1.0), and 'provenance' (same allowed values as `remember`); 'title', 'tags', and 'source' are optional (missing source is attributed to the calling client). Max 100 items.

arguments.name: agent_id
arguments.desc: Memanto agent identifier the memory belongs to (defaults to 'docker-test').

name: recall
description:
Search long-term memory for relevant context (semantic search, top-N results). Call this on your own, without waiting to be asked:
- at the start of a new task or topic, before writing code or running commands, to pick up the user's rules, preferences and earlier decisions
- when the user refers to earlier work ('like last time', 'the bug we fixed')
- before choosing a library, pattern or convention the user hasn't specified
- before asking the user for something they may have told you before
Use a natural-language query ('what are the user's rules for git?'), not keywords.

arguments.name: query
arguments.desc: Natural-language search query.

arguments.name: limit
arguments.desc: Max number of memories to return (1-100).

arguments.name: type
arguments.desc: Optional type filter - e.g. ['preference'] to only retrieve user preferences.

arguments.name: min_similarity
arguments.desc: Minimum similarity score 0-1. Applied by the search backend, so the top-N is filled with results that pass the threshold. Defaults to the server config value.

arguments.name: agent_id
arguments.desc: Memanto agent identifier the memory belongs to (defaults to 'docker-test').

name: recall_recent
description: Return the most recently stored memories (newest first). Use this to surface fresh context - e.g. 'what did we just decide?' - when you don't have a specific search query.

arguments.name: limit
arguments.desc: Max number of memories to return.

arguments.name: type
arguments.desc: Optional type filter.

arguments.name: agent_id
arguments.desc: Memanto agent identifier the memory belongs to (defaults to 'docker-test').

name: recall_as_of
description: Point-in-time recall: return only memories that were known before the given timestamp. Use this when the user asks historical questions like 'what did we know on 2025-11-01?' or to reconstruct context at a previous moment.

arguments.name: as_of
arguments.desc: Cutoff timestamp. Accepts YYYY-MM-DD (interpreted as end of that day) or full ISO 8601 e.g. 2025-11-01T14:30:00Z.

arguments.name: type
arguments.desc: Optional type filter.

arguments.name: agent_id
arguments.desc: Memanto agent identifier the memory belongs to (defaults to 'docker-test').

name: recall_changed_since
description: Differential retrieval: return memories created or updated after the given timestamp. Use this for 'what's new since X?' or to catch up on activity between sessions.

arguments.name: since
arguments.desc: Lower-bound timestamp. Accepts YYYY-MM-DD (start of day) or full ISO 8601 e.g. 2025-11-01T00:00:00Z.

arguments.name: type
arguments.desc: Optional type filter.

arguments.name: agent_id
arguments.desc: Memanto agent identifier the memory belongs to (defaults to 'docker-test').

name: answer
description: Ask a natural-language question and get an LLM-generated answer grounded ONLY in the agent's stored memories (RAG). Prefer this over `recall` when you need a synthesized answer rather than a ranked list, e.g. 'what did we decide about X?'. Returns the answer text plus the supporting memory sources.

arguments.name: question
arguments.desc: The question to answer.

arguments.name: limit
arguments.desc: Number of context memories to retrieve. Defaults to server config.

arguments.name: temperature
arguments.desc: LLM temperature. Defaults to server config.

arguments.name: kiosk_mode
arguments.desc: If true, refuses to answer when no memory clears the similarity threshold (useful for strictly grounded applications). Defaults to the server config value.

arguments.name: agent_id
arguments.desc: Memanto agent identifier the memory belongs to (defaults to 'docker-test').
